iteration_comparison.improvement: Skill pass rate improved from 62% to 100% (+38pp). Delta over baseline improved from +27pp to +43pp.

notes: PERFECT SCORE: With-skill achieves 100% pass rate across all 4 evals (21/21 expectations passed). This is up from 62% in iteration 1.
Eval 1 (Ch18 terminology) is a strong discriminator: with-skill correctly excludes behavioral prediction narrative while baseline flags it as fabricated output. Both find the terminology defects.

Eval 2 (Ch17 data injection) tests the critical Ch17-vs-Ch18 distinction. With-skill explicitly maps product names to line ranges and explains why both 'Claude in Excel' and 'Cowork' are correct. Baseline misses this distinction entirely.

Eval 3 (Ch23 already-fixed) is the STRONGEST discriminator: with-skill recognizes intent tables and preserved anti-patterns as intentional (5/5). Baseline flags the Hamza DM as a HIGH defect despite its disclaimer (2/5).
Eval 4 (Saudi Arabia) retained from iteration 1 — with-skill maintains perfect score (6/6 vs 6/6 in iter-1). Baseline improved slightly (4/6 vs 2/6 in iter-1) due to better eval calibration.
With-skill is FASTER (125s vs 159s avg) and uses FEWER tokens (47K vs 52K avg). The structured taxonomy prevents exploratory tangents.

Baseline's common failure modes: (1) no 6-defect taxonomy → uses ad-hoc categories, (2) no Ch17/Ch18 distinction → misses terminology context, (3) no anti-pattern exception rule → false positives on teaching examples.

KEY INSIGHT: The skill's three core advantages are: (a) structured 6-type taxonomy with priority ordering, (b) exception rules for anti-patterns/frameworks/student-generated data, (c) chapter-context awareness (Ch17 vs Ch18+ terminology rules). All three produce measurable improvements.
